newsitem.title: UK: Calluna up after director share buying.
newsitem.headline: Calluna up after director share buying.

text.p: Shares in disk drive maker Calluna Plc rose 26 percent on Monday after the company announced the purchase of stock by three of its directors.
The stock was up 7-1/2p at 35 by 1327 GMT in volume of just under 800,000 shares.

Managing director Norman White bought 50,000 shares, taking his stake to 3.725 million shares or 5.6 percent of the total, while finance director Donald MacDonald bought 40,000 shares to take his holding to just under half a million.
Sales and marketing director David Ruxton bought 16,000 shares to take his total stake to 863,440.
All three bought at 30p, though Calluna gave no further information.

Calluna shares dropped to an all-time low of 26p last week. The company earlier this month posted an increased pre-tax loss of 1.4 million stg in the past year, but said sales of its existing CT260 range were up 40 percent on the year before.
It said the pending commercial launch of its new Hardwall range "creates a new and potentially significant revenue channel."
